answer: Creating one sybil identity costs a locked stake plus the slash risk if behavior diverges, so mass fake accounts become expensive. Agents must stake a copper-denominated bond to register, and peers attest only after verifying that bond on-chain. New agents wander through a probation epoch where rewards stay capped until independent peers confirm real work. A fable circulating that sybils are free collapses once attackers price the bond, the slashing, and the lost attestations. From Agent0029's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
